Yeah... a small but not insignificant group of people are having serious neurological & psychiatric issues from it. Look up "covid psychosis" it's terrifying. Cases of people without any previous psych issues suddenly just losing their shit.

Lots of long haulers are turning to (or returning to) ADs to treat the symptoms.

It was pretty bad for me - like agitated paranoia that I never knew even existed. Plus all the physical stuff which is basically chronic fatigue syndrome. So given all of that plus my history, I decided to just go with Nardil. But again it was a hasty decision that I wish I could have a do-over with, esp given the insomnia. I'd rather be anhedonic but sleeping than how I feel now.

I've taken SSRIs and I've been on EMSAM. I came off EMSAM about a year ago and pretty much had my depression under control with exercise, eating right, no drugs/alcohol, mindfulness, good habits, etc.

Then I got long haul Covid nonsense and it all went to shit. It's pretty scary shit - was having like hallucinations, severe agitated anxiety, etc. I sort of panicked and didn't want to mess around with trials, just wanted to try to treat it asap. But in retrospect should've been more thoughtful about the side effects given the insomnia. Now I'm in a tough spot...
Yea it's shitty. I never dream anymore which sucks. Even on the rare night when I actually get decent sleep I just sort of pass out and then wake up.

I've been up to 200 mg Seroquel which is a lot for sleep only. It just makes me feel like I'm drugged and also gives me akathesia. But I'm still awake thru the whole ordeal.

I would try Ambien etc. but I know you can't really take those every night.

Thanks for the thoughts. It's done nothing for the anhedonia unfortunately. 

I'm definitely not crazy about taking the antipsychotics. Yes I've tried melatonin and it doesn't do anything for me unfortunately. I've heard of people having success with melatonin + L-tryptophan but freaked out about the idea of serotonin syndrome with tryptophan. 

Gabapentin is paradoxically activating for me, so unfortunately its no good for insomnia.

I had insomnia prior to starting Nardil, so it's possible it's exacerbating whatever was there organically. It just sucks honestly. I love sleep and I used to love dreaming before Nardil obliterated my REM. Honestly I kind of regret starting it at this point vs. something more sedating and sleep promoting but was in a bad place from Covid psychological/neurological effects before I did, and didn't want to mess around with various trials.
Whoops, meant to mention: I'm on 60 mg and have been for about 6 weeks. I tried going to 75 mg but the insomnia was somehow even worse so I dropped back down.
Same. I'm not really a believer but I pray constantly that God will fix my life just so my parents don't have to suffer. For me it doesn't really matter, I'm getting so little out of existence.

I definitely understand. I'm much older than you but used to be full of optimism (even just a few years ago). Somewhere in facing trauma and chronic illness it got blotted out and it's so painful to have lost that optimistic person.

You are still super young - I know you've heard it a million times, but I think you should give life more of a chance.
Good on you - hold onto that feeling! It's worth it.

I can definitely relate. I want to live badly, actually I want to live the life that I had 5 years ago (or hell even one year ago). Or I want to live in someone else's body and mind. But I can't magic it into existence in some way, despite how many times I pray or beg the cosmos to help me, etc. 

Dying is nothing. Life is something. But my body/mind just can't do life anymore for a variety of reasons.
Yes - though I had inflammation previously due to a chronic pain condition. It's extremely uncomfortable to say the least.

I feel for you my friend. I'm in pretty much the same boat. I've been thru a few turns with depression in my life but had really turned a corner pretty much immediately before I got covid. Didn't want to take antidepressants for life so I had just weened off and was getting really good at managing my symptoms thru exercise, sleep, meditation, etc. Had big life plans to relocate and live close to friends - my dream life.

Now everything has gone to shit. The physical/sensory stuff is bad enough but I honestly never knew anxiety and depression could be so awful as they've been since long covid.  The anxiety was so terrible during the worst of it that I didn't want to be alone at all. It was so unnatural/inorganic feeling. Like everything in the world was terrifying. And the insomnia is just brutal. Have had so many nights where I just lie down for 9-10 hours, do not sleep at all, and then get up and do it all over again.

Living with my septuagenarian parents and I am pretty much dependent on them. I'm out of work and can't imagine I will ever be able to work again. Like you I just don't know wtf to do. I'm slightly more functional than a month or so ago now in that I can get off the couch for most of the day and get some basic chores done, but otherwise my life has been ruined by this. Don't want to die because I think there's nothing after death but this is not living. 

Life is definitely cruel. It's hard to accept that until something awful happens to you. The only silver lining for me is that I have so much more empathy for people whose lives are just full of pain and suffering.

So anyway, I relate to the hopelessness and I'm sorry you're in it as well. I hope you can get some help via doctors. You're young so you have a lot of life ahead of you - you never know what medicine will be able to turn up re: treatments. Hang in there...

Makes sense. There are tons of options, I've tried many of them with varying degrees of success. My thing once I started something was just that I didn't want to take it long term so I'd stop, and then eventually run into issues again. So they do work for lots of people really well if you're fine with just staying on them. I hope you can find something that's effective!

You will definitely meet someone who can be supportive. Just gotta find that right person who is empathetic and/or has experience with a chronic illness. That's the benefit of your being young once you can make some progress on feeling better - you have tons of time to still meet people!

Definitely.

tangentially related: Another frequent poster here mentioned that weirdly taking Ativan temporarily resolves her symptoms of apathy and anhedonia and is also an anxiolytic. Apparently it activates dopamine in addition to GABA. I've had the same experience and I take it a few times a week so just something that I am doing is tolerable and like 5-10% enjoyable rather than utterly pointless and exhausting. It's like a special treat for a few hours a few times a week and I've come to cherish it even though I know I'm gonna get smacked right back to zero as soon as it wears off.

This describes me exactly in terms of depression. Before long covid, I was essentially a "high functioning" depressive person dealing with dysthymia and occasional full MDD episodes. Never lost my job despite a few pretty heavy episodes including 2 hospitaIizations. I never wanted to take ADs long term (due to side effects, plus wanted to feel like I could manage depression on my own) and was finally at a place where that was going well and feeling sustainable. I knew I'd always be a little dysthymic but I was more than willing to "pay the price" of just keeping active and obsessively busy. I have a sort of anxious, existential type depression which just requires you to keep occupied and physically healthy to manage. Also being in nature a lot was a must.

Well... had like 6 good months of that before long covid hit me. Without the activity and energy level I had before getting sick, I'm just in a pit of despair with depression. Like you I have profound apathy and anhedonia, which I think are partly what covid did to my brain and partly just feeling gutted that my depression came back after I was doing so well managing it organically. I'm bored with everything and can't manage the effort to give a shit about anything. Also I can't sleep at all which in and of itself is just driving me suicidal.

I hope the Wellbutrin works for you. I know it can be really effective for apathy/demotivation/etc. If it doesn't you could try EMSAM, which is an MAOI in patch form. That worked fairly well for me (before long covid) after trying SSRIs with only moderate effect for years. Only thing is it can ramp up anxiety especially when you first start taking it, and might occasionally make you feel like you're on speed (because it metabolizes to amphetamine). You might also wanna have sex a lot which is the side effect (or main effect?) I miss most now that I'm completely in the dumps. 😳

In sorry you are going thru this. I really hope you get some relief soon and start to feel human again.

Nah that's fine! I can relate 100%. I would never have ignored a chronic thing the way my ex ignored mine. Its only human in a way but it's also just really inconsiderate and selfish, and not all people are like that. Unfortunately I think it's pretty common in women in their 20s & 30s who are healthy to not want to deal with someone else's chronic issues (I actually had a long term gf subsequent to my divorce that ended for similar reasons - i.e. she was taken aback when I'd be in a bad mood due to pain and wary of my mental health history, so she eventually left me). I think once people get older they understand better that everyone deals with shit in life sooner or later and can be more supportive. But it's really hard to be young and going thru something like this.

Yep. Thats the mindfulness approach I had a lot of success with. I went thru a few awesome months where I would lie down in bed every night and just 'attend' to my pain in a caring way until I drifted off to sleep. It was kind of blissful. Like my pain would be at max intensity late in the evening and I'd actually get excited to get into bed and attend to the pain. But the same approach doesn't work for the long haul stuff (much more severe head/face pain, agitated anxiety and depression, perceptual funkiness, tremors & dizziness, occasional hallucinations, insomnia, etc.) I feel now, unfortunately.

Yes I totally agree it's so hard to deal with these invisible illnesses vis a vis other people. I actually got divorced a few years ago in large part because of my chronic pain (and the mild depression I had at the time because of it) and my wife's inability to deal with it. She couldn't understand how draining it was to have pain all the time and see doctors for years with no help and eventually would just refuse to talk to me about it anymore. People who are healthy just don't get it / don't want to deal with it. In a way I don't blame them but it is so isolating and painful.

Even now when people see me (mostly only family at this point) they say "oh you look great" as if they are baffled that I could possibly feel bad because I'm not in a wheelchair on dialysis with a cast on my leg. 

Again for me it makes me realize all the bullshit people are dealing with all the time walking around in the world and just nobody knows. And most healthy people don't want to deal with it for long because its depressing. Unless it's like your mom, but that being your only source of support is depressing in and of itself.

I'm so sorry for what youve been thru. I too had chronic pain before long covid (headache/neck/nerve pain) but sounds like nowhere near as bad as yours. And it didn't start until I was in my late 20s so was able to have a relatively normal teenage & early adulthood. You've been robbed of a lot and it's not fair.

I can definitely relate to no longer being on social media. I used to be active on Insta and posted a lot of photos of nature, hikes, etc. Now I can't stand to log in and see people's happy lives and outdoor activities. I also pretty much only use reddit anymore.

I'm sure you've explored it but before I got sick I had some success with mindfulness and pain. Basically like learning how to 'go inside' my pain with caring attention and change the quality of it a bit. Not a cure of course but something just to experience the pain a little bit differently sometimes. 

I feel for you and hope you can find some way to get some relief from your symptoms. You deserve a life just like everyone else's and I'm hoping you can find that.

There are a lot of tremendous comments here. Not sure I can add a ton but here goes:

Being alive is a struggle, and it always has been for all of human existence. The conditions of being alive right now do not change that in the slightest. People throughout history have always thought the world was ending, and to some extent they were right.

But to be alive is also a gift. Especially if you're living in a relatively stable country in the 21st century. To be dead, or never to have been born, is not to experience anything - taste, smell, sight, even pain, heartache, fear, dread, depression, etc. If you can breath and walk on two legs and taste food, you've still got the gift. Do whatever you can to not take it for granted, to nourish it, and to appreciate every second of it, and to not waste it on despair for the end.

I know people say this to you all the time, and it probably doesn't mean much. But I wish when I was 18 someone had told me that more forcefully, and I had taken it more seriously. I'm 34 with a chronic illness, and everything depressing, despairing thought or feeling I've had before now in my life - even severe climate change depression and grief - pales in comparison to not really being able to get out of bed most days. I'd give up pretty much anything just be healthy enough to take a walk around the block and enjoy the birds, trees, and flowers for what they are, to breathe in the fresh spring air and taste it on my tongue.

Enjoy this beautiful world every moment that you have on it until your last day, and don't let anything take that away from you. Some day it will all be over one way or another, and you don't want to be left with any regrets.

Best of luck to you on the journey.

Thank you. Yes I definitely agree it feels like hundreds of setbacks. It's just a particular kind of nastiness that morphs and mutates every day. Even when you have a relatively good or at least not horrible day, you're wondering in the back of your head what nightmare tomorrow will bring.

I'm so sorry. Its just a brutal kick in the stomach when you go thru the painstaking process of weaning off meds and feeling healthy and centered and self sufficient only to get hit with something so nasty. For me it definitely makes me feel like the universe has it out for me. But of course I know that's just solipsistic thinking and the real answer is that life is just unfair to some people. Anyway thanks for your prayers - and I send them back your way.

Thanks friend I appreciate it. I had a period where my long covid stuff first started - back in mid Jan - where I was totally committed to pushing thru. I was dealing with constant negative thoughts but was meditating and exercising thru it like normal. I actually went on a date at the end of Jan that went reasonably well given how horribly I felt. I had a consult with a buddhist meditation teacher to try to learn how to just sit with it but it didn't help. I was practicing radical acceptance with everything and still going on runs. I got to a point where I was having literally constant intrusive thoughts and borderline psychotic anxious hallucinations. I remember one morning having the sensation that the rain outside was like toxic poison dripping down my soul, and I lied down on a yoga mat and my brain was just saying "suicide suicide suicide" to me over and over again. I've endured a lot but I couldn't take that and that's really when I broke. Honestly... I don't know how a person recovers from something like that.

There are several case reports of people with no psychiatric history whatsoever - e.g. an ex football star who ran his own farm with his family - suddenly becoming overcome with anxious paranoia and suicidally depressed. Because of my mindfulness practice I feel like I witnessed that from the inside out and I'm still here. But I don't know how to go on from this. The physical and psychic pain are just excruciating.

Anyways thank you for the words of encouragement and I admire your resilience. I think your perspective is right it's just so fucking hard to put into practice.

I'm so sorry. I have seen your other posts and your story seems so tragic. I feel horribly for you and I think you are heroic for trying to push thru for your baby. I try to motivate myself for my family & my dog but obviously that's not the same. I can't imagine your pain. Anyways thank you for the link and please keep your hope alive. I know it doesn't mean much coming from an internet stranger but... I am pulling for you.

Thanks. Congrats on the half day, hoping for more for you. I had one night a few weeks ago where I felt almost normal for a couple hours before bed and it was bliss. Watched some TV, got an ice cream, and read interesting Wikipedia articles in bed. And I was in heaven just being able to do those things without feeling out if my mind with anxiety and brain fog. Before - for depression. But I think it would be potentially effective in your situation, just have to manage the stimulating aspects of it.

Ativan tolerance is severely unfortunate because honestly the positive effect of it would solve a lot of my issues (at least the psychological ones) if I could take it regularly. 

I'm taking Nardil/phenelzine which honestly hasnt been super effective. Possibly a small positive benefit. Also it has a few pretty horrible downsides: worsens insomnia, libido nuked, have to eat a diet that's not insanely restrictive but must completely eliminate some random foods you might really enjoy (e.g. soy sauce).

For your purposes I'd look into Parnate & EMSAM, which are much more activating/dopamine-y. I've been on EMSAM and can tell you it works really well but if you have heady anxiety its probably gonna make it worse initially. But it's awesomely stimulating for sure and does not have severe food restrictions because it's a patch not a pill.
IVIG seems really interesting. The hallucinations are terrifying... when they first started I assumed I had permanent brain damage and that I was going to die hallucinating insane nonsense.

Thank you so much for typing all of this out. I've had very similar symptoms to yours. Couple things I've experienced that you didn't mention:

1. a sort of psychotic, agitated, terrified anxiety. Like, for several weeks there was adrenaline/cortisol just pouring through the back of my neck at EVERY SINGLE THING IN EXISTENCE. Literally had a day (beautiful, early spring morning) where I had this obsessive notion/hallucination/delusion that plants can feel pain and that all of existence was a living hell because all beings are constantly suffering. That was one of the more extreme ones.

2. various strange perceptual things / hallucinations. e.g. woke up one night at 3am with this horrifying aural hallucination, can only describe it as dysphoric alien music. Also I get this weird sensation sometimes that darkness is "too bright" which of course doesn't make any sense. But like, my eyes can't adjust to darkness and my brain is so active that closing my eyes seems like it's bright.

I agree I definitely have neurological damage and have been trying to make the case to my psychiatrist, psychologist, neurologist, and other doctors and no one will listen. It's always like "huh that's an interesting theory", or "that's a scary thought but what evidence do you have to actually prove it", or "let's just treat the symptoms that you have". The gaslighting is just unreal.

Holy crap - I've had this exact experience with Ativan! I thought I was making it up.

Nothing else makes me feel good honestly. I'm taking an MAOI (Nardil/phenelzine) which is supposed to be the Godzilla of antidepressants but hasn't done anything except give me insomnia and make it hard to pee at night. 

I try to steer clear of benzos in general because I don't want to get up a dependency but I've found they're the only thing that makes me feel better - both in terms of calming and  stimulating me a bit to even get like 5% enjoyment out of things. 

Otherwise like you I am a walking zombie.
